newsitem.title: TURKEY: TURKISH BROKERS KEEP CALM DESPITE ERBAKAN'S WORDS.
newsitem.headline: TURKISH BROKERS KEEP CALM DESPITE ERBAKAN'S WORDS.

text.p: Prime Minister Necmettin Erbakan's threat of early elections is unlikley to trigger a strong wave of selling in the afternoon session of the Istanbul Stock Exchange as price have already bottomed out, brokers said.
"The market will probably show a negative reaction to his words. But reaction buyings might follow sales soon at low prices," said Berra Kilic, assistant general manager of Ata Securities.
The IMKB Nationaal-100 ended 0.83 points higher at 1,453 after a 5.9 fall in the past three days.

"Today at any moment, whoever wants it, we are ready for elections," Erbakan told his Islam-based Welfare Party (RP) amid intensified opposition efforts to bring down his coalition with the conservative True Path Party (DYP).

Brokers say Istanbul shares which posted minor gains in Tuesday morning session following recent losses prompted by political concerns have fallen to very low levels overall which they say might be attractive for buying.

Bulent Ecevit, leader of Democratic Left Party, is holding talks with other opposition leaders on forming a government excluding the RP, at odds with army over the implememntation of anti-Islamist measures.

On Saturday, Erbakan reluctantly agreed to demands from the army for a series of anti-Islamist measures, but his Islam-based Welfare Party has made it clear it was not prepared to go along with reforms that would close Koranic schools.
"Destroying fundamantalism is of life or death importance," General Kenan Deniz told a special briefing for journalists.
